title: YouTube Music removes Samples tab from its bottom bar on Android and iOS
summary: Samples tab, you will (not) be missed.
body: Credit: Roydon Cerejo / Android Authority TL;DR YouTube Music is removing the Samples tab from the bottom navigation bar on Android and iOS via a server-side update, leaving three tabs for Premium users and four for free users. The vertical Samples feed is still available on individual artist, album, and playlist pages via a “Sample this” card or the Samples icon in the top-right. Google is also widely rolling out an album and playlist redesign previously spotted in October, featuring larger cover art and rearranged action buttons. YouTube Music is decluttering its mobile app by removing the Samples tab from the bottom navigation bar on Android and iOS. While the TikTok-style vertical discovery feed is no longer front and center, the company is also rolling out a broader interface refresh that overhauls album and playlist layouts and rearranges key playback controls. With the Samples tab gone from the main navigation bar, YouTube Music Premium subscribers are left with just three bottom tabs: Home, Search, and Library. Free users still see a fourth Upgrade tab on the far right. According to 9to5Google , the change is rolling out gradually via a server-side update.

title: Harry Styles, Sam Fender & Billie Eilish to Headline Glastonbury Festival 2027: See Lineup
summary: The festival will take place from June 23-27 in Somerset, England.
body: Harry Styles , Sam Fender and Billie Eilish will headline the 2027 edition of Glastonbury Festival . The announcement on Wednesday (Nov. 18) includes the headliners for the first edition of the English festival since 2025 as well as a number of the expansive undercard. The festival will take place between June 23-27, with the full music programme running on Friday, Saturday and Sunday (June 25, 26, 27). Harry Styles and Sam Fender are first-time headliners at the event, with Eilish returning following her maiden headline appearance on the Pyramid Stage in 2022 ; in doing so, she became the festival’s youngest-ever solo headliner. It has not yet been confirmed which respective day each will perform on. Cher will perform in the Legend’s Slot on Sunday afternoon, traditionally held for iconic artists. Previous performers include Lionel Richie, Rod Stewart and the late Dolly Parton. Joining them on the lineup so far is Massive Attack, Sombr, Little Simz, Chase & Status, The xx, Lily Allen, Ezra Collective and Kraftwerk. Additional names are Adéla, Angine de Poitrine, Atarashii Gakko!, The Avalanches, Basement Jaxx, Blood Orange, Bonobo, Christine and the Queens, Chvrches, Co…

title: YouTube’s new ‘co-view’ count for TV estimates the number of people watching TV at once
summary: By guessing the total number of viewers in front of the TV.
body: Credit: Ryan Haines / Android Authority TL;DR YouTube will now start showing a new “co-view” count on all videos watched on TV. This new metric accounts for multiple people watching on the same set at the same time, for both long-form videos and Shorts. It says the new metrics will help creators gauge their true reach on TV. YouTube is taking a page out of digital broadcasters ‘ playbook and adding a new view metric that will be publicly available. This new metric is called “co-view,” and it estimates the total number of people who watched a particular video while accounting for multiple people watching on a single TV set. With this, both Shorts and long-form videos will now display the number of co-views alongside a regular view count . Co-views are exclusive to YouTube’s TV app and won’t appear on mobile or desktop. Co-view data will be available starting today, and won’t apply to older views. However, it will apply to all existing and new videos on the platform.

summary: Live Nation, OVG and Plenary will build the arena, which will have an 18,700 capacity in concert mode and which, the team behind it say, should bring more major live events to the city.
body: BRISBANE, Australia – The capital of the Sunshine State, Brisbane, will become a two-arena city when a new 17,000-capacity venue is completed ahead of the 2032 Summer Olympic and Paralympic Games. A years-long wait for approval came to end this week when Gather Brisbane was rubber stamped, a major new live music and entertainment project for the inner-city suburb of Woolloongabba. Live Nation, OVG and Plenary will build the arena, which will have an 18,700 capacity in concert mode and which, the team behind it say, should bring more major live events to Brisbane. According to forecasts presented by Live Nation, the arena is expected to welcome more than 1.2 million people each year, support upwards of 1,500 ongoing jobs and generate almost A$844 million ($568 million) annually for the city’s visitor economy. “Brisbane has the audience and the ambition to welcome more of the world’s biggest tours, but it needs the venues to match,” comments Michael Coppel, chairman of Live Nation Australia and New Zealand. “This arena will help bring more shows to Queensland, strengthen Australia’s appeal as a touring destination and give artists and fans an arena they can be proud of for decades t…

body: Credit: Xiaomi TL;DR Xiaomi has launched the Xiaomi Clip earbuds in global markets. The Xiaomi Clip also supports the LHDC 5.0 codec, Apple’s Find My network, and audio/video/call recording by triple-tapping the case. title: Oura Ring’s new Jet Lag feature helps you adjust to different time zones
summary: Your body clock might finally be ready for its next vacation.
body: TL;DR Oura’s new Jet Lag feature uses your sleep history and chronotype to create personalized plans for adjusting to different time zones. It recommends when to get sunlight, avoid bright light, sleep, and cut off caffeine, while tracking your recovery and offering post-trip insights. The feature is rolling out globally for Oura Ring Gen 3 and newer users. Traveling to a new country is exciting, but jet lag? Not so much. You could land in the morning, ready to explore, only to find yourself struggling to stay awake a few hours later. And when it’s finally time to sleep, your body might have other plans. Oura wants to make those first few days a little easier with its new Jet Lag feature, which uses your sleep data to help your body adjust to a different time zone. It looks at your sleep history and chronotype (your body’s natural sleep and wake preferences) to create a personalized plan. It also estimates when your body reaches its lowest temperature, typically around 4 AM, to better understand your internal sleep cycle.

body: Credit: Robert Triggs / Android Authority TL;DR Samsung appears to be testing smarter automation features in the SmartThings app, along with agentic capabilities. With this upgrade, SmartThings could offer deeper insights, combine multiple routines into one, suggest better automations, and even help cut your energy bills. Samsung may also allow third-party AI agent services, such as ChatGPT Codex, to let them control devices remotely. We’ve recently learned that Samsung is working to overhaul AI features on its Galaxy smartphones and tablets and give them agentic abilities. Earlier this week, we discovered tons of evidence surrounding Galaxy Claw , a framework that would allow phones to run tasks across the system as well as third-party apps with minimal human supervision. However, it looks like Samsung may not limit these agentic AI features to mobile devices, but also extend them to smart home appliances.

The Android emulation and native port scene is moving at breakneck speed, with Banana Native now running 10 Nintendo Switch 2 games on Android devices. Building on recent momentum around Switch 2 emulators and native ports on Android , the latest updates expand the project’s compatibility list to seven officially supported titles, including Mario Kart World, Donkey Kong Bananza, and Pokémon Pokopia, along with three experimental games. title: Android Time Machine lets you try Android 2.1 through 7.1 right in your browser
summary: Time to go on a nostalgia trip.
body: TL;DR Android Time Machine is a website that simulates old versions of Android right in your browser. It currently has eight releases, from Android 2.1 Eclair to Android 7.1.2 Nougat. Each version runs on the Nexus phone it originally shipped on, and there’s nothing to install. Android is by far the most popular mobile operating system out there. However, the Android we see today is very different from what it was years ago, back when Google still named it after desserts (and not just codenames, either) and things like Material 3 Expressive weren’t even on the radar. If you’ve ever wondered what Android was like before gesture navigation, expandable notifications, or even an on-screen back button, a new website could scratch that itch. Android Time Machine (spotted via 9to5Google ) is a web-based project that lets you run old versions of Android in your browser. The site, built by developer szabolevi98, currently offers eight Android releases, starting with Android 2.1 Eclair on the Nexus One and going all the way to Android 7.1.2 Nougat on the Nexus 6P.

title: I tested Pixel 10 Extreme Charging, but there’s nothing extreme about it
summary: Google brings faster charging to the Pixel 10 series, but should you use it?
body: Credit: Robert Triggs / Android Authority Google’s November Pixel Drop is here , packed full of new AI, customization, and other features to upgrade your Pixel experience. The update also brings Extreme Charging Mode, fresh from the latest Pixel 11 series, to last year’s Pixel 10 range. If you’re not familiar with it, Extreme Charging aims to speed up your Pixel’s charging by pausing some background tasks, creating a little more breathing room for charging power and heat. I wasn’t too impressed when Extreme Charging debuted on the Pixel 11 series . Even before using it, the feature was arbitrarily disabled until I’d charged the phone a couple of times. Once finally enabled, Extreme Charging traded higher temperatures for shaving about five minutes off the phone’s total charge time; a controversial trade-off in my book.

title: Wear OS watches can now use your phone’s GPS to save battery life
summary: There's finally a reason to carry your phone with you on your outdoor workouts.
body: TL;DR Google has released v26.45 of Google Play Services. It lets your Wear OS watch use your phone’s GNSS to track location during outdoor workouts, which helps conserve watch battery life. The Play Store v54.1 also adds the Pixel virtual gamepad for compatible games when your Pixel Fold is open. If you often use your Wear OS smartwatch to track outdoor workouts, you may be aware of the impact it can have on battery life. Google is now rolling out a new feature that should help. Google has released a new version of Google Play Services (v26.45) that adds a feature letting your watch use your phone’s Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) to track your location during outdoor workouts. GNSS is a term for satellite-based positioning systems, such as GPS, Galileo, GLONASS, and NavIC. Running the watch’s GNSS receiver for an entire workout uses a lot of battery. By offloading that job to your smartphone, Google wants to make your watch’s battery last longer. Fitbit already offers something similar on some of its trackers with its Dynamic GPS feature.

title: US cities have some of the world’s weakest indoor mobile signals, Ookla finds
summary: Better indoor reception starts with better outdoor coverage.
body: TL;DR A new Ookla study ranks North America among the worst-performing regions globally for indoor 4G signal strength. Weak indoor signals affect 41% of measured buildings in Miami, 38% in Los Angeles, and 25% in New York, compared to just 2% in Seoul. Weak outdoor coverage explains about 85% of the differences in indoor signal strength between cities, although dedicated in-building cellular equipment can significantly improve reception. Much has been made of the strides US carriers have made in improving their networks, with recent reports highlighting everything from faster download speeds to wider 5G coverage . But those improvements may not mean much when you’re struggling to upload a photo from your living room. New research suggests American cities have some catching up to do when it comes to delivering reliable mobile coverage inside buildings. A new report from Ookla analyzed a year’s worth of mobile signal measurements across more than 100 cities in 60 countries. North America ranked alongside Oceania at the bottom for indoor 4G signal strength, trailing not only East Asia and the Middle East but also Africa and Latin America.

title: Apple brings camera-based Face ID to iPhone Duo, but too bad it didn’t copy Pixels
summary: Apple is following Android OEMs by offering camera-based face unlock on the iPhone Duo.
body: Credit: Aamir Siddiqui / Android Authority TL;DR Apple has brought camera-based Face ID to the iPhone Duo as part of the second iOS 27.3 beta. Unlike the Pixel’s face unlock, Apple’s solution doesn’t support purchases, adding passwords/logins, and other tasks. In other words, this is the standard camera-based unlock seen on the majority of Android phones. Apple released the iPhone Duo last month and, like many Android foldables, it comes with a side fingerprint scanner. That’s a significant change from recent iPhones, which all have Face ID via dedicated sensors. However, Apple is taking another page out of the Android playbook by adding camera-based Face ID to its first foldable phone. The iPhone Duo has received camera-based Face ID in the second iOS 27.3 beta, as spotted by MacRumors . The outlet notes that you need to have recently authenticated your device via fingerprint scanner or passcode entry to use face unlock. Furthermore, you’ll need to scan via Touch ID after 45 minutes of inactivity.

title: Motorola confirms some Signature 27 buyers will get a much smaller battery
summary: Local battery regulations are to blame.
body: TL;DR Motorola has confirmed to Android Authority that Germany is getting the Signature 27 with a different battery configuration. The German variant packs a 5,500mAh battery instead of the 7,000mAh unit available in other markets. Motorola attributes the downgrade to local lithium battery regulations affecting transportation and logistics. A massive 7,000mAh battery is one of the biggest selling points of the Motorola Signature 27 , a phone that packs just about everything you’d expect from a modern Android flagship. But as we discovered last week, not everyone buying Motorola’s latest premium smartphone will get to enjoy that headline-grabbing battery capacity . We now know where and why. In a statement to Android Authority , a Motorola spokesperson confirmed that the company is using a different battery configuration for the German market due to local regulatory requirements.

body: Credit: Edgar Cervantes / Android Authority TL;DR Google has added .docx support to the Compare documents tool. This update allows users to compare .docx files directly in Google Docs without having to convert them first. Support is available for Workspace customers, Workspace Individual subscribers, and users with personal Google accounts. Google has started rolling out an update to Calendar that allows you to pick which end of a meeting you want to put your five-minute buffer on. However, that’s not the only Workspace-related update that’s available today. The tech giant is also rolling out a Docs update that makes comparing documents more convenient. While Google Docs allows you to view and edit Microsoft Office files without converting them first, that wasn’t true if you wanted to use the Compare documents tool. Not only did this force you to convert the file, but it also resulted in you having unnecessary duplicate files in your Google Drive. Those problems are being solved with the rollout of .docx support for the Compare documents tool.

title: Google Maps expands Ask Maps with itineraries, list search, and appointment booking
summary: The update starts rolling out today.
body: TL;DR Google Maps Ask Maps adds itinerary creation, list search, and appointment booking. The update rolls out today, with some features available only in the US. Google is expanding Ask Maps to over 30 countries in Europe, including Spain, Germany, and the UK. Google Maps introduced Ask Maps to help casually answer questions using Gemini, and now it’s getting three new features that help you make an itinerary, search your lists, and schedule appointments. With air travel more unpredictable than ever, it’s likely more people will be hitting the road instead of taking to the skies this holiday season, so these upgrades come at a good time. Planning an itinerary with Ask Maps can cover an afternoon of hitting stores to finish up all your holiday shopping or a multiday trek across several states. No matter what type of trip you’re setting up, Ask Maps will put numbered pins on the map for each stop along the way. For long excursions, it can create a schedule for each day with recommendations and tips for every stop. After everything is set up, you can share the plans with others, or if you love seeing an itinerary on a page, export it to Google Docs.
